The self-declared size band is 11-50, above the count; nothing published puts the team at 11 or more, so the count is used as it stands, and it is a small team. Iterative says it invests between US$150,000 and US$500,000 per company rather than one fixed cheque, so the amount is counted as a sized round. rows.verify_note: Test 1 (venture-built): Sokratech was founded by Brian Lee, a former data scientist at Shopee, OVO and GoCardless (Tech in Asia, 9 Mar 2026). It sells its own fraud-detection platform to banks, payment gateways and fintechs on annual enterprise subscriptions or per-transaction pricing, is backed by the Iterative accelerator fund (Summer 2024 batch), and is not part of any bank or group. Test 2 (own entity): PT Sokratech Teknologi Indonesia is in the Indonesian company register (AHU registration number 1892349 on the companieshouse.id mirror, status recently active, registered at Gedung Wirausaha Lantai 1 Unit 104, Jl. HR Rasuna Said Kav. C-5, Jakarta Selatan), and it is the name under which Sokratech is listed as an exhibitor at Telecoms World Asia 2026 (Bangkok, 27-28 Oct). The site itself names no legal entity. Test 3 (headcount): LinkedIn shows 6 people on 2026-10-10 against a self-declared band of 11-50; the count is used. Geography: the LinkedIn page gives Singapore as its headquarters and main location, with Jakarta as a second location, and Brian Lee's own profile is set to Singapore. The row is counted in Jakarta because the team and the operating business are Indonesian: the four software engineers who list Sokratech on their LinkedIn profiles are in Jakarta and Depok (one gives his role as Jakarta-based, with on-site deployments at a bank client); the only legal entity found is the Indonesian PT, whose registered address is used here because the company publishes no street address of its own; Brian Lee wrote on LinkedIn (9 Jun 2025) that he left GoCardless in the UK "to build something from scratch in Jakarta"; the product is built around Indonesian payment rails (BI-FAST, SKN, RTGS, QRIS) and OJK and Bank Indonesia rules, with an Indonesian-language blog and LinkedIn page; Tech in Asia says it is live with commercial banks, payment gateways and fintechs in Indonesia; and its 2026 programmes, events and partners are Indonesian (OJK Fintech Accelerator, ASWIFTINDO, IAFPC Jakarta, Q2 Technologies, Smartcoop, Lintasarta, Jatis Group). Liveness: sokratech.io answered 200 on 2026-10-10 with a 2026 copyright, a privacy policy updated in July 2026 and a July 2026 blog post; the LinkedIn page posted on 29 and 30 Sep 2026; in 2026 the company was featured by Tech in Asia (March), presented its product at ASWIFTINDO (April), sponsored and exhibited at IAFPC Jakarta (July), ran a webinar with Q2 Technologies (28 Aug), presented at the OJK Fintech Accelerator programme (company post of 10 Sep), announced a partnership with Smartcoop (14 Sep) and is listed to exhibit at Telecoms World Asia (October). Doubtful: the team is small, the Singapore headquarters line on LinkedIn (which matches only the founder's own location) is not explained by any source, and Brian Lee's LinkedIn title is "Co-Founder & CEO" although no source names another co-founder. The founding year 2024 comes from Brian Lee's LinkedIn profile (co-founder and CEO since April 2024) and Iterative's Summer 2024 batch; the PT's registration date was not checked. Namesakes: no other company trading as Sokratech was found; similarly named registered companies (PT Skortech Karya Indonesia, PT Ratech Teknologi Indonesia) are unrelated. Brian Lee is a common name; the founder is the former Shopee, OVO and GoCardless data scientist whose LinkedIn profile lists Sokratech (Iterative S24).

Test 2 (own entity): PT Perisai Sistem Keamanan is named in the footer and About page of perisai.id, the company's Indonesian-language site (same phone number and contact@peris.ai address, linking to peris.ai and the same LinkedIn page), and on retas.id, its red-team page ("PT Perisai Sistem Keamanan / Est. 2024", contact at peris.ai). Metro TV News (31 Oct 2025) and Suara (1 Nov 2025) name PT Perisai Sistem Keamanan as the company behind Peris.ai, quoting founder and CEO David Samuel. The procurement marketplace Mbizmarket lists PT Perisai Sistem Keamanan as a verified, VAT-registered (PKP) vendor in Cengkareng, Jakarta Barat, a member since 12 Aug 2026. The peris.ai site itself names no entity. Test 3 (headcount): LinkedIn shows 31 people on 2026-10-10, band 11-50. Geography: the LinkedIn page gives Singapore as headquarters, and peris.ai lists offices in Jakarta, Singapore (160 Robinson Road, SBF Center) and Abu Dhabi (Masdar City incubator building). The row counts the company at its Jakarta address because the company, its PT and its leadership are Indonesian: Liputan6 (17 Sep 2026) calls it a local cybersecurity company and Warta Ekonomi and Suara (Oct-Nov 2025) an Indonesian startup; East Ventures called it Indonesian-based; the CEO's LinkedIn profile is in Jakarta; the Jakarta address is listed first on the site and in its Organization schema; and the clients named in its testimonials are Indonesian (JIEP, RRQ, Modal Rakyat) plus Telkomcel in Timor-Leste. No source names a Singapore company. The building's street address (Jl. Lingkar Luar Barat No. 101, Rawa Buaya, Cengkareng, 11740) is from Tokopedia's own contact page; peris.ai gives "Tokopedia Care Tower Lt 16, Jakarta Barat (11740)". Liveness: peris.ai answered 200 on 2026-10-10 with a 2026 copyright; the LinkedIn page posted about Brahma Fusion about 20 hours before it was read; in September 2026 Peris.ai received the IN-Apps Digital Award 2026 for cybersecurity technology platforms from the Ministry of Creative Economy (Liputan6, 17 Sep 2026), and it won Startup of the Year at the ASEAN Business Awards 2025 in Kuala Lumpur (Warta Ekonomi, 31 Oct 2025). Doubtful: Warta Ekonomi's version of the October 2025 release names the company "PT Perisai Digital Indonesia"; the company's own Indonesian site, Metro TV, Suara and Mbizmarket all say PT Perisai Sistem Keamanan, which is used here; no company-register record for either name could be read. retas.id dates the PT to 2024, while LinkedIn gives 2022 and the East Ventures round came in February 2023, so the 2023 money may have gone into an earlier or holding entity; no source says which. Floor 16 of Tokopedia Care Tower is shared with BizWork, a virtual-office and coworking provider (unit 16.39), so the Jakarta address may be a serviced office; where the team works day to day is not published. Namesakes: "perisai" (shield) is a common Indonesian word, and several unrelated Indonesian companies carry it in their names (for example PT Perisai Andalan Sakti and PT Perisai Optima Global in Jakarta Selatan and PT Perisai Aman Nusa in Bandung); the company itself trades as Peris.ai, Perisai and Perisai Cybersecurity and also runs perisai.id, retas.id and cyberbreaker.id (its Cyber Breaker Competition CTF).

rows.verify_note: Test 1 (venture-built): Prospero is founder-led and sells its own software. Bobby Yulandika Putra, previously risk management division head at Bank of India Indonesia, financial risk country manager at AIA and in sharia risk policy at BTPN, founded it and runs it as CEO (UIII, 18 May 2026; APAC Entrepreneur, 22 May 2025); Paul-Adrian Mandravel joined as co-founder and CTO in 2025 (UIII; the company's LinkedIn page). Its product is an enterprise risk-management (GRC) platform, launched as Pro ERMS in Oct 2022 after a soft launch with two banks (Republika, 28 Oct 2022) and now sold on-premise or as a cloud plan from US$350 a year; APAC Entrepreneur names BTPN Syariah, Bank Syariah Indonesia, BNI Life, BRI Finance and HiBank as users. It also earns from risk training and certification (Prospero Learning Academy) and consulting, so part of the business is services, but it is not an agency or reseller. It went through Accelerating Asia's Cohort 10 (Oct 2024), a VC accelerator that takes a stake, and Startup Studio Indonesia. Test 2 (own entity): PT Prospero Optima Solusindo. The company's former About page said Prospero Solutions operates "under the name of PT. PROSPERO OPTIMA SOLUSINDO"; that page went offline when the site was rebuilt, and the current site and LinkedIn page do not print the PT name. The AHU mirror companieshouse.id lists PT. Prospero Optima Solusindo as an active limited liability company, number 781727, registered at Talavera Office Park lantai 8, Jl. TB Simatupang Kav. 22-26, South Jakarta, with a constitutional amendment on 10 Oct 2022; the EMIS company database dates its incorporation to 28 Nov 2016. Test 3 (headcount): LinkedIn shows 6 people on 2026-10-10, band 11-50. Geography: an Indonesian company run from Jakarta. The LinkedIn page gives its head office as DKI Jakarta, and UIII interviewed the founder after he returned to Jakarta from the May 2026 award. The address used is the PT's registered office from AHU; a Google Maps listing that links to the site places a Prospero Solutions office at Plaza Mutiara lt. 8, Jl. DR. Ide Anak Agung Gde Agung Kav. E.1.2, Kuningan Timur, Setiabudi, Jakarta Selatan 12950, in the same city. The site calls Singapore a "regional hub for ASEAN & international growth" after Block71 Singapore and Echelon Asia 2025, and says a reseller partner is signed in Malaysia, but it gives no foreign address or entity; its clients, regulators and phone line are Indonesian. Liveness: prosperosolutions.co.id answered 200 on 2026-10-10 with a 2026 copyright and a cloud plan "launching in August 2026". In 2026 the company was the Southeast Asia winner of the Global Startup Awards and Bobby was named Founder of the Year at its Grand Finale in Malta on 8 May (UIII); it won two WealthBriefingAsia Greater Awards (company LinkedIn post, 28 May) and was a finalist for the IIRSM Risk Excellence Awards (company LinkedIn post, 3 Jun). Doubtful: the founding year. The LinkedIn page gives 2016, matching the PT's 2016 incorporation, but UIII quotes Bobby as founding Prospero "as a solo venture in 2022", the year the software launched; no source explains the gap, and 2016 is used here. The LinkedIn count (6) is below the page's own 11-50 band. EMIS gives the same PT a head office in Probolinggo, East Java, which no other source supports. Namesakes: the "Prospero" chocolate drink from an Indonesian cocoa exporter; Prospero Indonesia (prosperoindonesia.com), an advertising agency in Matraman, Jakarta Timur; a LinkedIn page called Prospero Solutions based in Ho Chi Minh City; Prospero, a Melbourne financial-services firm; and PT Optima Solusindo Informatika, a Jakarta IT distributor.

rows.verify_note: Test 1 (venture-built): Restock.id is a founder-built fintech, founded in 2019. Its named co-founders are Muhammad Farid Andika, co-founder and CEO until April 2021 (Hybrid/DailySocial, 3 Feb 2021; CNBC Indonesia, 3 Apr 2021), and Rega Sardjono, co-founder and now a director (Hybrid/DailySocial; Kontan, 1 Dec 2025). It raised a US$1 million seed round in 2020 led by the local venture firm Tunas Nusantara Kapital with Silverbacks Ventures and angel investors (Kontan, 22 Feb 2021). It runs its own lending platform, which finances small and medium businesses against their stock and business assets with money from individual and institutional lenders. In 2019 its majority shareholder was Cerita Investasi Amanah Pte. Ltd., which Kontan described as an investment company owned by young Indonesians from finance and fashion retail; since 2022 it has been a 99.9% subsidiary of the group holding company, PT Cerita Restock Teknologi Amannah Tbk (RestockTech, set up in 2020), which also runs warehouses and owns the IT company Revota (PT Ava Revota). The holding's 2025 shareholding chart lists Muhammad Audi Vialdo (73.84%), Tiar Nabilla Karbala (16.80%) and Rega Prasidhagiwa Sardjono (9.36%). According to the company blog (15 Mar 2022), Tiar Karbala came in as an early funder and investor in 2019, when Rega was planning Restock.ID, became a commissioner in mid-2020 and took over as CEO in April 2021; Kontan's seed report quotes "Tiar" as founder of the lead investor, Tunas Nusantara Kapital. Test 2 (own entity): PT Cerita Teknologi Indonesia is named on the site's contact page and on its audited financial statements for 2019 to 2025, and by Kontan (1 Dec 2025) and SWA. It was registered with OJK in Aug 2019 and licensed under OJK decision KEP-52/D.05/2021 of 2 Jun 2021, per the company's blog. Test 3 (headcount): LinkedIn shows 27 people on 2026-10-10, band 11-50. Geography: head office at Sequis Tower Level 19 Unit 7, SCBD, Jakarta Selatan, per the site's contact page and LinkedIn; the holding's site gives Level 19 Unit 6B in the same tower. The 2019 Singapore parent did not take the business out of Indonesia: the team, licence, borrowers and lenders are Indonesian, and the parent since 2022 is an Indonesian company. Liveness: restock.id answered 200 on 2026-10-10 with lending statistics updated that day (Rp376.8 billion disbursed in 2026, Rp3.76 trillion repaid to date, Rp317.5 billion outstanding). Its LinkedIn page posted on 6 Oct 2026, it held a "Coffee Club" business community event in Bandung on 27 Aug 2026, and it announced a partnership with Boleh Dicoba Digital in Dec 2025 (Kontan). The site's server sends an incomplete TLS certificate chain, so some strict clients refuse to connect while browsers load it. Doubtful: the seed size. Co-founder Rega Sardjono told DailySocial on 3 Feb 2021 that the seed was US$750,000 from unnamed local investors, while the company's announcement three weeks later (Kontan) gave US$1 million with named investors; the later figure is used. The holding calls itself a "Tbk" (public) company and its site carries investor-relations pages, but no listing or share offering was found, and its shareholding chart shows only three individual owners. That chart names the subsidiary "PT Cerita Restock Indonesia", while the site, the audited accounts and the press all use PT Cerita Teknologi Indonesia. Namesakes: Ninja Xpress's "Ninja Business to Business Restock (B2BR)" logistics service is unrelated; RestockTech and Revota are group companies, counted here only through Restock.id.

rows.name: Assemblr
rows.sector: Edtech — no-code 3D and augmented-reality (AR) creation platform: Assemblr EDU gives teachers and students curriculum-aligned 3D/AR lesson kits, a 3D editor, visual coding and classroom tools (monthly plans for individual teachers, school plans, and premium access for Indonesian teachers and students who sign in with official belajar.id accounts under a ministry partnership), alongside Assemblr Studio for general creators, the LessonCrafts AI lesson-planning workspace, and custom 3D/AR projects for brands' marketing and staff training

rows.employees_note: LinkedIn lists 40 people on the company page ("Lihat seluruh 40 karyawan"), read 2026-10-10 on id.linkedin.com/company/assemblrworld; the page links to assemblrworld.com, and it is also the page Assemblr's investor Insignia Ventures Partners lists. The self-declared size band is 11-50, which fits the count, and the page's headquarters line is Bandung, West Java. Assemblr EDU appears as a product on this page; no separate LinkedIn company page for Assemblr EDU, Assemblr Studio or LessonCrafts was found, so the count is not split between pages. It may include a few people at the Singapore affiliate and the Malaysian subsidiary; no country split is published. No 2026 company statement of headcount was found.
rows.funding_note: Two outside investments on record, one of them sized. Seed, 2018 (amount not disclosed): founder and CEO Hasbi Asyadiq wrote on the company blog (25 Jan 2019) that he began raising a seed round in November 2017 and closed it with a VC six months later; the blog's third-anniversary post (28 Feb 2021) says the investor came from Singapore and that the money paid for the Dago office the company moved into in August 2018. Insignia Ventures Partners lists Assemblr in its portfolio as a partner since 19 June 2018, stage "Early"; no amount has been published. Ficus Capital, December 2022 (US$400,000): the Malaysian shariah-compliant venture firm invested through its Ficus SEA Fund, its first investment outside Malaysia (Business Today, 8 Dec 2022; Katadata, 9 Dec 2022, about Rp6.2 billion; Disruptr, 9 Dec 2022). The Edge Malaysia (27 Jan 2025) and Disruptr (16 May 2025) describe the same investment as funding a Malaysian subsidiary, Assemblr Studio Sdn Bhd. Only the Ficus amount is summed, so US$0.4M is a floor. Not counted: accelerator places on standard terms (Techstars Hub71 in Abu Dhabi, January to April 2021; Plug and Play batch 6 and the SYNRGY Accelerator batch 2, both completed in April 2020; Facebook Accelerator Singapore season 2, 2020) and Y Combinator's free Startup School (2018). Tracker context only: CB Insights and Indexed.vc show US$550K raised in total, including a US$150K "seed" attributed to Techstars Ventures in February 2023; no announcement of it was found.
rows.valuation_note: No publicly reported valuation. CB Insights shows a December 2022 valuation that no announcement or reputable outlet carries; it is not used.
rows.verify_note: Test 1 (venture-built): Assemblr began in 2017 as a prototype that Hasbi Asyadiq built while at Octagon Studio, a studio he had co-founded as CTO in 2014, and became a separate company in July 2018 after a seed round from a venture investor (company blog, Jan 2019 and Feb 2021). Hasbi is founder and CEO; Anita Yustisia (CCO) and Risnandar (CTO) are co-founders (company blog; Katadata, Dec 2022). Insignia Ventures Partners lists Assemblr in its portfolio since June 2018, and Malaysia's Ficus Capital invested US$400,000 in December 2022. Octagon Studio is not a bank, conglomerate or listed group, and Assemblr has been a separate company with its own investors since 2018. Assemblr sells its own platforms (Assemblr Studio, Assemblr EDU and the LessonCrafts AI tool, on monthly and school plans) and builds custom 3D/AR projects for brands such as BCA, Ducati and Dekoruma on top of them, so it is not an agency or reseller. Test 2 (own entity): the Assemblr Studio terms of use (effective 14 Oct 2022) say the service is provided by PT. ASSEMBLR TEKNOLOGI INDONESIA, "based in Indonesia", and its Singapore affiliate (written there as "Assemble Pte Ltd"; the site footer names Assemblr Pte Ltd). Test 3 (headcount): LinkedIn shows 40 people on 2026-10-10, band 11-50. Geography: the terms give the company's office as Jl. Ir. H. Juanda No. 477 (Ruko Blok D), Dago, Coblong, Bandung 40135, the address LinkedIn shows as the main location; the About page says the team is "from Bandung, Indonesia", LinkedIn's headquarters line is Bandung, the site's phone number is a Bandung (022) number, the company's 2025 MIT Solve entry gives Bandung as the team's headquarters, and the blog says the Dago office has been its home since August 2018. The site footer lists only Singapore addresses, for Assemblr Pte Ltd, which the terms call an affiliate; no source says which entity owns the other. The row is counted at the Bandung office, where the team and the product are. A Malaysian subsidiary, Assemblr Studio Sdn Bhd, followed the Ficus investment. Liveness: assemblrworld.com answered 200 on 2026-10-10 with a 2026 copyright. In 2026 Assemblr EDU opened to students with belajar.id accounts (July), was listed in the Learning Cabinet catalogue of reviewed EdTech tools (September), and runs ImajiNation 2026, a national visual-coding competition with the Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education and Samsung, which reached judging in late September; it also posted hiring calls in mid-2026. Doubtful: the founding year is 2018 in the company blog (separate company from July 2018, platform launch on 28 Feb 2018) and in Katadata, but 2017 on the LinkedIn page; 2018 is used. The LinkedIn page's company-type field says "Public company", but no source mentions a share listing. Gaby Wantah, the COO, is called a co-founder in a Women's Tabloid interview (Oct 2025) that the company's LinkedIn page reposted, but the company's own founding accounts do not name her. Namesakes: Octagon Studio is the founder's earlier company, not Assemblr; the Android app still carries Octagon Studio's package name.

rows.name: Lentera App
rows.sector: Media — Indonesian e-book reading app: a curated digital library of novels, short stories, poetry, textbooks, self-help and religious titles, earning from low-priced reader memberships, single-book purchases and in-app advertising, and paying authors and publishers a royalty for every page read; also runs writing competitions and the SoraSore readers' community
rows.hq_address: Satrio Tower Building, 12th floor, Jl. Prof. Dr. Satrio No. 7, Blok C-5, Kuningan Timur, Setiabudi, Jakarta Selatan
rows.employees_note: LinkedIn lists 12 people on the company page ("Lihat seluruh 12 karyawan"), read 2026-10-10 on id.linkedin.com/company/lentera-app; it is the page lentera.app links to, and it links back to www.lentera.app. The self-declared size band is 2-10, slightly below the count. The count may include outside contributors rather than staff: the company recruits teachers and writers as contributors, the founder advertised remote sales-affiliate roles in January 2026, and the one profile the page shows publicly is a teacher who also works as a writer and translator. No company statement of headcount was found.
rows.funding_note: No outside money on record: no announced equity round, grant or loan was found on the company's site, in the founder's posts or in the press. The founder wrote on LinkedIn in January 2026 that the app had started charging users a small fee and had "finally made money". Programmes, not funding: Lentera.App was one of eight startups, out of 162 applicants, picked for InnovateHer Academy 3.0, a mentoring programme for women-led startups run by KUMPUL with FWD Insurance and UN Women Indonesia (KUMPUL announcement, 3 Oct 2025); the programme offers mentoring and access to investors, and no investment in Lentera was announced. The company also entered the Startup World Cup 2023 pitch competition (founder's post, July 2023).
rows.verify_note: Test 1 (venture-built): Lentera is a founder-led startup: Annastasia Puspaningtyas founded it and runs it as founder and CEO (the company's own launch article, Sept 2023; Hypeabis, Oct 2025). It sells its own reading app, with memberships and book sales, rather than services, and no source reviewed names a parent company or corporate shareholder. Test 2 (own entity): PT Lentera Metamesta Nusantara is named as the operator of lentera.app and the Lentera app in the terms of service (updated 6 Apr 2022) and privacy policy (updated 18 Aug 2022) on the site, and as the developer and copyright holder of the iOS app on Apple's App Store; the site footer reads "Copyright © Lentera Metamesta Nusantara". Test 3 (headcount): LinkedIn shows 12 people on 2026-10-10, band 2-10. Geography: the company's contact page gives Satrio Tower Building, 12th floor, Jl. Prof. Dr. Satrio No. 7, Blok C-5, Jakarta Selatan, with no postcode; the Jakarta governor's 2019 decree on Satrio Tower places the building in Kelurahan Kuningan Timur, Kecamatan Setiabudi (it gives the lot as Kav. C.4). LinkedIn's headquarters line is Jakarta, and the Ministry of Creative Economy's EKRAF Hub lists the product under Jakarta Selatan. Liveness: lentera.app answered 200 on 2026-10-10. The iOS app had 12 releases in 2026, the latest on 3 Oct 2026 (version 2.4.2), adding QRIS memberships in January and book purchases in July; the Android app, with 10,000+ downloads, was updated on 28 Sep 2026. In January 2026 the founder said the app had started charging, was running a 2026 writing competition with GoTo, and was recruiting sales affiliates. The website itself has not been updated since October 2023; the apps carry the current product. Doubtful: no source states a founding year, so none is given. The founder's LinkedIn profile dates her founder role to October 2021, and the app was launched publicly at the Indonesia International Book Fair in September 2023 (company article; VOI, 29 Sep 2023). Namesakes: "Lentera" is a common name. This row is not the Yogyakarta furniture exporter Lentera, not Flip (PT Fliptech Lentera Inspirasi Pertiwi), not Binar Academy's PT Lentera Bangsa Benderang, and not other registered companies with Lentera in their names (for example PT Lentera Nusantara Gemilang or PT Lentera Media Nusantara); lenteraapp.com is not the company's site. The company spells the founder's first name Annastasia; she also goes by Anna.

The site's partner page offers dispenser hosts and brands rental, revenue-share, sponsorship and white-label deals; those are sales, not investment. rows.verify_note: Test 1 (venture-built): Mari Isi Ulang (MIU) is a small founder-led company, not an incumbent's unit. Its CEO, Andhika Dirgantara, describes himself on LinkedIn as founder and CEO of the Sustainable Intelligence Dispenser (SID) and, per the same profile, has led PT Bersih Hijau Lestari since July 2022; no outside investor is on record. It sells its own branded product rather than an agency service: SID dispensers that sell drinking water by the litre into people's own bottles, paid by QRIS with a refill pass sent over WhatsApp, offered in three models to malls, offices, campuses, events and public spaces for rent, sale, revenue share or corporate sponsorship, with impact reporting for the hosts. It is a hardware-and-service business with light software (payments, refill passes, an impact dashboard), and it sells drinking water only, not household goods. Test 2 (own entity): PT Bersih Hijau Lestari is named in the mariisiulang.id footer and on its contact page ("Kantor Pusat PT. Bersih Hijau Lestari"), and in the About section of the LinkedIn company page; no public registry extract was found to confirm the registration. Test 3 (headcount): LinkedIn shows 3 people on 2026-10-10, band 2-10. Geography: head office at Jl. Cimanuk No. 11a, Citarum, Bandung Wetan, Kota Bandung 40115, per the site's contact page and the LinkedIn page. Liveness: mariisiulang.id answered 200 on 2026-10-10 with a 2026 copyright and seven blog posts dated 29 Aug to 28 Sep 2026. Doubtful: no press coverage of the company was found, so this row rests on its own site, its LinkedIn page and its CEO's profile. The site's own reach figures disagree with each other (42,500+ plastic bottles saved in one panel and 420,000 in another; 120 dispenser locations on the home page and "500+" refill stations on the product page), so none is used here. No source gives a founding year: the site says MIU has been developing its product since 2023, and the CEO dates his role at PT Bersih Hijau Lestari from July 2022. Namesakes: PT Jabar Bersih Lestari (a West Java waste-to-energy partnership company), PT Jaya Bersih Lestari (Clean it Up, waste collection) and PT Hijau Lestari Prakarsa Utama (waste processing) are unrelated companies; the domain mariisiulang.com no longer answers.

rows.verify_note: Test 1 (venture-built): DoctorTool is founder-led. Its About page, company profile and March 2024 press release name Rainaldo (CEO and co-founder), Septu Jamasoka (CTO and co-founder) and Elisa Yoshigoe Wijaya (CCO and co-founder); dr. Gatot Soetono, a former director of Pertamina Hospital and board member of the Indonesian Medical Association, is chairman and chief medical officer. It sells its own products: the SIM Faskes clinic-management and electronic-record system, the DT Hub device and the DTCare patient app; Fortune Indonesia (18 Dec 2024) reported its generative-AI prescribing and note-taking support, built on IBM watsonx. No equity investor and no parent company are on record; the UN Global Compact lists PT Medifa Infoyasa Suryantara as a privately held SME, and its outside support is a DBS Foundation grant (March 2026) plus accelerator places. Test 2 (own entity): PT Medifa Infoyasa Suryantara is named in the doctortool.id footer, terms of use and privacy policy, in the company's own press releases (such as the one dated 26 Sep 2025), in IBM's partner directory and in the UN Global Compact participant list. Test 3 (headcount): LinkedIn shows 42 people on 2026-10-10, band 11-50. Geography: the site gives the head office ("Kantor Pusat") as Galeon Square Lt. 8 Unit A, Jl. M.H. Thamrin No. 9-10, Kebon Melati, Tanah Abang, Jakarta Pusat 10230, used here, and an operations office at Jl. Cipinang Cempedak II No. 35A, Jatinegara, Jakarta Timur 13340. LinkedIn gives the HQ as Jakarta Pusat ("Jl. MH Thamrin No.8-9 Plaza Galeon, Lt.8"), and IBM's partner directory lists the same floor, unit and street number under the name Chubb Square. Liveness: doctortool.id answered 200 on 2026-10-10. The site's newest blog post is from December 2025, but its impact-report page was updated in June 2026, and the LinkedIn page is active: on 10 Oct 2026 it posted about sponsoring a Universitas Indonesia nursing-faculty event, and in the days before it announced a second prize at the 5th Healthy Aging Prize for Asian Innovation and a place in the 2026 Reckitt Catalyst cohort. DBS Foundation named it a grantee in March 2026. Doubtful: the founding year. The site ("Sejak tahun 2015", with operations starting in 2015, development from 2016 and a commercial launch in 2019), the LinkedIn page and Fortune Indonesia give 2015, while Tracxn and Dealroom give 2011, which no primary source supports. Reach figures grow with the date of each statement: 1,000+ facilities in 34 provinces (LinkedIn product text), 2,000+ (Sep 2025) and 2,500+ in 37 provinces (Oct 2026). Namesakes: doctortool.com is a parked domain for sale, not the company's.

rejected_record.name: Sanggabiz
rejected_record.why: Fails test 1: Sanggabiz (PT Sangga Bisnis Anda) is mainly an outsourcing and consulting business that sells its team's work, not a product of its own. It markets itself as 'Department as a Service': bookkeeping and financial-report packages priced by monthly transaction volume, tax consulting, audits with a partner public accounting firm, recruitment, payroll, staff placed with clients (its August-October 2026 openings include on-site QRIS and EDC field sales reps, housekeeping and customer-service officers, several marked 'Coverage: Eksternal'), customer-service and call-centre teams, digital marketing, market research and consulting (its site hosts a 2026 organisation-restructuring study for PDAM Tirtamarta, Yogyakarta's water utility) and corporate training. LinkedIn files it under Business Consulting and Services, and the press calls it a technology-based business consulting company (youngster.id, 24 Sep 2026). Its AI offerings are sold as managed services: SanggaChat is a chatbot that Sanggabiz's own team sets up, trains and monitors for clients (LITE to UNLIMITED+ packages), and AiTax is offered 'by Sanggabiz Consulting' as a revenue-forecasting method piloted with Yogyakarta City's finance agency (BPKAD). Its first self-service software, Sanggabright (an analytics app for SMEs), only entered a beta pilot in October 2026 (company release, Nusantara Pos, 9 Oct 2026). No venture or angel round is on record: the only outside money is programme support, a UGM Startup Grant 2026 Batch II at incubation stage, run by UGM's Innovative Academy with the higher-education ministry under the ADB-funded PRIME STeP project, which gives grants of up to Rp12 million (youngster.id, 24 Sep 2026); the company's release credits that programme with funding Sanggabright's development. It pitched to investors at UGM's Capital Room event on 4 Sep 2026; no round has been announced. The other checks, for the record. Test 2 would pass: PT Sangga Bisnis Anda, AHU business number 1282252, registered at Sendari, Jalan Bambu Gading No. 111, Kabupaten Sleman, DI Yogyakarta (companyhouse.id AHU mirror), and named in its 9 Oct 2026 release and in UGM careers-office job posts. Test 3: LinkedIn lists 55 people ("Lihat seluruh 55 karyawan"), band 11-50, HQ line Jakarta, founded 2022, read 2026-10-10; the count is slightly above the band and probably includes freelancers and staff placed with clients, and its UN Women's Empowerment Principles profile self-declares 51-200 employees. Geography: the site footer and LinkedIn say Jakarta, but its own 2026 releases say it is based in Yogyakarta ('berpusat di Yogyakarta'), the PT is registered in Sleman, and most openings are in Yogyakarta; it is Indonesian either way. Liveness: sanggabiz.com answered 200 on 2026-10-10, with blog posts up to 6 Oct 2026, active LinkedIn and job posts; the older Canva site sanggabiz.co.id also answers. Founder and CEO: Dwi Andi Rohmatika. Revisit if Sanggabright becomes a paid product that carries the business, or if the company raises an outside round. Namesakes: Sangga La (an agroforestry corridor project) and Sanggau Regency are unrelated; Bromo Today (4 Apr 2026) spells it 'Sangga Bis'.
